messages:
emily: Quick sync — thinking about the onboarding cadence for the bench/acceptance step. current thought: fast tile checks + periodic full bench. opinions?
raj: +1 to tiles. full bench is expensive and delays rollout. what's a tile in this context?
marta: Tile = a deterministic subset of golden prompts across domains. we shard by prompt family and sequence length. 3 tiles covers short/med/long.
kevin: How often do you want the full bench vs tiles? nightly full bench sounds expensive.
emily: Proposal: run 1 tile smoke per merge -> immediate signal. run all 3 tiles on canary starts. full bench (all golden inputs + negative tests) nightly for admitted models.
ciara: Sounds reasonable. what about acceptance thresholds? p99 latency, token generation divergence, and sample-level QA score?
raj: We need concrete numbers. suggest p99 <= baseline * 1.15, top-1 token KL divergence < 0.05 on golden sets, and human-eval delta below 3% for baseline tasks.
marta: For KL we should use smoothed KL on token distributions across seeds, not raw. also allow model-type-specific baselines (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder).
kevin: Interface boundary question: does the ingest pipeline own tiling logic, or does bench-orchestrator decide which tile to run?
emily: Prefer bench-orchestrator to own scheduling. ingest should surface metadata (model family, max-seqlen, quantized flag, weights fingerprint).
ciara: Agree. keep an explicit contract: ingest -> {metadata, model-binary, signature}. bench-orchestrator -> pulls artifacts and runs selected tiles. keeps retry/backoff.
raj: That means a small refactor: move tile-selection from ingest service into bench-orch. low-risk but touches CI wiring.
marta: Also want shard-wise smoke tests that run inside runtime to catch ABI/KV-cache regressions — those should be super-fast (sub-1s per sample). benchbot: AUTOMATED: added shard-smoke job template to bench-orch (run-time quickcheck).
kevin: For runtime regressions we need end-to-end golden replay tests that exercise kv cache warmup. these live in the canary stage.
emily: Tradeoff note: moving scheduling into bench-orch increases coupling but reduces duplicate logic. rollout plan: land bench-orch API first (ingest can call old endpoint), migrate tiling in a follow PR.
ciara: Observability: bench runs must emit token-level diffs, latency histograms, and an acceptance boolean. these get indexed to onboarding-dashboard.
raj: Important: acceptance boolean should be conservative. default: fail on any p99 regressed by threshold OR any QA delta > configured. humans can then triage.
marta: Add a soft-fail mode for experimental branches so we collect metrics without blocking. toggle via ingest metadata flag: experimental=true.
kevin: What about quantized variants? we should run tile checks on both fp16 and quantized if artifacts provided; if quant only, ensure we have quant-compatible smokecases.
emily: Good point. bench-orch will try compatible variants if available; otherwise it falls back to baseline model. routing policy documented in bench-orch README.
ciara: Action items: 1) emily/raj design bench-orch API + tiling spec 2) marta add shard-smoke job template 3) kevin add kv-warmup golden scenarios 4) emily open migration PR for ingest callers.
emily: I'll draft the API spec today and post it. PR for migration Thursday?
raj: I'll sketch acceptance thresholds and put them in params.yaml. we should allow per-team overrides.
marta: I'll add sample lists for the 3 tiles and a script to extract families from golden corpus.
kevin: I'll wire the kv warmups into canary pipeline.
benchbot: REMINDER: weekly bench-cost report runs every Monday 04:00 UTC.
ciara: Thanks all. this feels actionable. if no objections I'll start the RFC follow-up doc with the decisions and the migration plan.
emily: No objections. cc: @product for visibility when we have thresholds.
ciara: End.
